Topic1.Title: Opening remarks on Boulder Valley School District resilient school plan and city property interest
Topic1.Summary: Council Member Benjamin noted BVSD passed a resilient school plan and asked city staff about discussions on possible city uses of district properties. City Manager Nuria Rivera-Vandermyde said the city is discussing with the district possible uses such as a police substation or training center, and will return to council with any proposals.

Topic2.Title: Public safety update: police staffing, public safety information center, and crime trends
Topic2.Summary: Police Chief Steve Redford reported the department is authorized for 190 sworn officers and is currently 12 short, with about 30 unavailable for solo deployment. Dispatcher and records staffing were also discussed. Redford highlighted the new Public Safety Information Center, rising proactive policing, declining property crime, and rising assaults, along with drug, financial crime, and officer assault examples.

Topic3.Title: Council questions on police staffing, Flock-style camera integration, retention, e-bikes, and care team
Topic3.Summary: Council asked about the Boulder Community Connect program integrating private cameras into the public safety center, retention strategies including facilities and cost of living, drug enforcement limits, the CARE team changes, and e-moto or e-bike enforcement. Staff explained that camera sharing is voluntary and that many departing officers cite housing costs and facilities. Requests for disaggregated race data and care team outcomes were made.

Topic4.Title: Police oversight: complaint classification, demographics, panel activities, and five-year review
Topic4.Summary: Independent Police Monitor Sherri Dean presented 2025 complaint data, including 149 allegations and 18 sustained findings, along with demographic breakdowns and panel turnover. Panel co-chairs Lizzy Friend and Bill De La Cruz raised concerns that new intake gateways have reduced cases reaching the panel. A five-year review of the oversight system is underway, with a report expected in October.

Topic5.Title: Municipal court data on unhoused defendants, community court, and young adult cases
Topic5.Summary: Presiding Judge Jeff Khan and Court Administrator Devon Kiss-Kelly reviewed municipal court data showing citations to unhoused defendants, the community court diversion program with hundreds of dismissals, and warrant and in-custody trends. They also covered young adult cases such as MIP, nuisance parties, noise, and fraudulent ID, with increasing large amplified party concerns on the Hill and coordination with CU.

Topic6.Title: Sister cities program resolution update
Topic6.Summary: Assistant City Manager Pam Davis and City Clerk staff presented proposed updates to Resolution 631 to clarify application, review, annual reporting, and deactivation processes for sister city alliances. Staff recommended an online application, clear review timelines, deadlines for council consideration, standardized agreements, and a possible cap or formal deactivation process. Council generally supported a council committee to oversee the program, a possible cap, and an escalating compliance process.
